title: Finite-coefficient Cech primitives lift with prescribed reduction
statement:
Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $q:T\to S$ be a continuous surjection of profinite spaces, meaning compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces. For $r\geq1$, let $P_r=\{(t_0,\ldots,t_{r-1})\in T^r:q(t_i)=q(t_j)\text{ for all }i,j\}$ with the subspace topology, as in [def-sfb-profinite-cech-tuples]. For a topological abelian group $M$, write $C^k(M)=C(P_{k+1},M)$ for all continuous maps, with pointwise addition, and for $k\geq0$ define
$$(d_k^M c)(t_0,\ldots,t_{k+1})=\sum_{j=0}^{k+1}(-1)^j c(t_0,\ldots,\widehat{t_j},\ldots,t_{k+1}),$$
where the signs act by the additive group law. Let $n\geq1$, let $A,B$ be finite abelian groups with the discrete topology, and let $p:B\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjective homomorphism. Suppose $c\in C^n(B)$ satisfies $d_n^B c=0$, and a prescribed $u\in C^{n-1}(A)$ satisfies $d_{n-1}^A u=p\circ c$. Then there exists $v\in C^{n-1}(B)$ such that
$$p\circ v=u,\qquad d_{n-1}^B v=c.$$
The empty surjection $T=S=\varnothing$ and the zero coefficient groups are included; in particular, $A=0$ gives a continuous primitive for every finite-$B$-valued positive-degree cocycle. No continuous section of $q$, and no homomorphic section of $p$, is assumed.

proof.text: Identify positive-length scalar tuples with the existing set Cech nerve by retaining the same coordinates; both directions are continuous and commute with deletion. Build the continuous alternating boundary from the continuous deletion maps. Apply the differential-squared clause of [lem-weil-pbc-set-cech-nerve-free-resolution] over the integers to a basis tuple, then apply Finsupp.linearCombination with the given cochain as coefficient function. This proves the continuous cochain boundary squares to zero. Additive coefficient homomorphisms commute with the signed sums. These formulas also apply to empty spaces without choosing a point.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.9(2), (4), printed page 33; agent-written explicit finite-kernel correction, using finite Cech descent and the finite-set contraction.

proof.text: Choose a set-theoretic section $s:A\to B$ of the surjection $p$, so $ps=\mathrm{id}_A$. Since both groups are discrete, $s$ is continuous; it need not be additive. Set $t=s\circ u\in C^{n-1}(B)$, so $pt=u$. Let $K=\ker p\subseteq B$ with its subgroup law and discrete subspace topology, and let $i:K\hookrightarrow B$ be inclusion. It is a finite abelian group. Put $e=c-d_{n-1}^Bt$. Then $pe=pc-d_{n-1}^Au=0$, so $e=i\circ e_K$ for a unique continuous $e_K:P_{n+1}\to K$. The cancellation in step 1 and $d_n^Bc=0$ give $i\circ d_n^Ke_K=d_n^Be=0$; injectivity of $i$ gives $d_n^Ke_K=0$.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.9(2), (4), printed page 33; agent-written explicit finite-kernel correction, using finite Cech descent and the finite-set contraction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-valued-cech-cocycle-descent] to $e_K$ in degree $n$. Its spaces are the original compact Hausdorff totally disconnected $T,S$, and its map is the given continuous surjection $q$. Its coefficient group is the finite discrete abelian subgroup $K=\ker p$; step 2 gives continuity of $e_K$ and $d_n^Ke_K=0$, and the item assumes $n\geq1$. Obtain finite discrete $T_0,S_0$, continuous surjections $a:T\to T_0$, $b:S\to S_0$, and a surjection $q_0:T_0\to S_0$ with $q_0a=bq$. The returned $e_0:(T_0)_{S_0}^{n+1}\to K$ pulls back to $e_K$ and satisfies $d_ne_0=0$ on every quotient tuple. This last conclusion is used directly; it does not require a quotient tuple to lift to $P_{n+2}$.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.9(2), (4), printed page 33; agent-written explicit finite-kernel correction, using finite Cech descent and the finite-set contraction.

proof.text: Choose a section $\sigma:S_0\to T_0$ of $q_0$ and put $w_0(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})=e_0(\sigma(q_0(x_0)),x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})$. All entries have the same $q_0$-image. Evaluate $d_ne_0=0$ at $(\sigma(q_0(x_0)),x_0,\ldots,x_n)$: its first term is $e_0(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$, and its remaining sum is $-d_{n-1}w_0(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$. Here deleting $x_0$ uses the same inserted point because $q_0(x_1)=q_0(x_0)$; $n\geq1$ ensures $x_1$ exists. Thus $d_{n-1}w_0=e_0$. This is a function on a finite discrete space, hence continuous.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.9(2), (4), printed page 33; agent-written explicit finite-kernel correction, using finite Cech descent and the finite-set contraction.

proof.text: Define $w(t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1})=w_0(a(t_0),\ldots,a(t_{n-1}))$. The relation $q_0a=bq$ makes this well-defined on $P_n$, and its coordinate formula makes it continuous. Coordinatewise $a$ commutes with every deletion, so $d_{n-1}^Kw$ is the pullback of $d_{n-1}w_0=e_0$, namely $e_K$. Set $v=t+i\circ w$. Then $pv=u$ since $pi=0$, and $d_{n-1}^Bv=d_{n-1}^Bt+i\circ e_K=c$. The argument allows $K=0$, $A=0$, or $B=0$; in particular $A=0$ yields the asserted finite-coefficient primitive.

(1) If S is empty, T and every cochain group are empty or zero because n>=1; d^2=0 because the signs (-1)^{i+j-1} and (-1)^{i+j} cancel. (2) With a set section s of p and t=s∘u, e=c-dt has pe=pc-du=0, so it factors through K=ker p, and de_K=0 because the inclusion of K is injective; additivity of s is never used. (3) The current statement of lem-sfb-finite-valued-cech-cocycle-descent matches item for item: T and S compact Hausdorff totally disconnected, q a continuous surjection, M=K finite discrete, n>=1, e_K continuous with its cocycle equation. It returns surjective a and b, q0 with q0a=bq, the factorization, and the cocycle equation on every quotient tuple. It does not depend on this item, so there is no cycle. (4) For w0(x)=e0(σq0x0,x0,...,x_{n-1}), evaluating de0=0 at (σq0x0,x0,...,xn) gives e0=dw0; this uses q0x1=q0x0 and n>=1. (5) For w=w0∘a^n and v=t+i∘w: pv=u and dv=dt+e=c. I checked the edge cases n=1, empty spaces, K=0, A=0, B=0, the non-split Z/4→Z/2 and q=id.
